intro: English has one little verb for I am. Spanish has two. When you say who you are, where you are from or what you are like, you use ser: Soy Maya. Soy de Chicago. When you say how you feel or where you are right now, you use estar: Estoy cansada. Estoy en la escuela.

In this unit you will read a pen-pal letter from Monterrey and spend a long day at a county fair. You will learn the five forms of each verb, match -o and -a endings, and ask ¿De dónde eres? and ¿Cómo estás?
By the end you will be able to introduce yourself, describe a friend, say how you feel, tell where you are, and choose between ser and estar with a simple rule of thumb.
bigQuestion: Why does Spanish need two verbs for to be, and how do you know which one to use?

words.d: to be — who you are, where you are from, what you are like, your job
to be — how you feel and where you are right now
they are, you all are (estar) — Están en la escuela.
in, at — Estoy en la casa.
happy, glad — a feeling, used with estar
nice, friendly — a trait, used with ser

test.q: Choose the right word: Yo ___ de Puerto Rico.
test.why: Where you are from uses ser, and yo takes soy.

test.q: Choose the right word: Hoy nosotros ___ cansados.
test.why: A feeling today uses estar, and nosotros takes estamos.

test.q: What does Ella es mi amiga mean?
choices: She is at my friend's house.
She is happy with my friend.
test.why: Ella es means she is, and mi amiga means my friend.

choices: Mi mamá es en la casa.
Mi mamá está en la casa.
test.why: Where someone is uses estar: está en la casa.

test.q: How do you ask a friend How are you?
test.why: ¿Cómo estás? uses estar and asks how someone feels.

test.q: A boy says he is tall. Which is right?
test.why: Tall is what you are like, so use ser, and a boy takes -o.

test.q: Which is spelled the Spanish way?
test.why: Nationality words are lowercase, and a group adds -s.

test.q: Choose the right word: Tú ___ muy inteligente.
test.why: Smart is a trait, so use ser, and tú takes eres.

test.q: What does Chicago está en Illinois mean?
test.why: Estar plus en tells where a place is.

test.q: Sara is sad today. Which is right?
test.why: A feeling today uses estar, and Sara takes está.

test.q: Which form of estar goes with ellos?
test.why: Ellos, ellas and ustedes take están.

test.q: My uncle is a cook. Which is right?
test.why: Jobs use ser with no un, and a man is cocinero.

test.q: Which question asks where someone is from?
test.why: ¿De dónde eres? uses ser and de to ask where you are from.

test.q: Leo y Ana ___ en la feria.
test.why: Where people are uses estar, and two people take están.

test.q: What is the rule of thumb for estar?
choices: Use it for your name and job.
Use it for where you are from.
Use it for how you feel and where you are.
Use it for what you look like.
test.why: Estar is for how you feel and where you are right now.

write.prompt: Write 4 to 6 sentences in Spanish to introduce yourself to a pen pal. Say who you are and where you are from (ser), what you are like (ser), how you feel today (estar), and where you are right now (estar).
tips: Use soy for your name, where you are from and what you are like.
Use estoy for how you feel and where you are.
Match -o or -a on each describing word to you.
Check accents: estás, está, están, and ¿De dónde?
Read it aloud to a partner before you finish.
